translations.source_sense_description: получить в обмен на деньги или иные ценности

glosses: To obtain (something) in exchange for money or goods.

examples.text: Who'd Father buy the car for? He boughtit for me, not for you.
Buy what thou hast no need of, and ere long thou wilt sell thy necessaries.

glosses: To obtain, especially by some sacrifice.

examples.text: I've bought material comfort by foregoing my dreams.
You just bought yourself an assault charge!
Buy the truth and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.

glosses: To suffer consequences for (something) through being deprived of something; to pay for (something one has done).

examples.text:
VVhat villaine, doſt ſtrike me? I ſweare by the rood,
As I am Iacke Strawe, thou ſhalt buy it with thy blood.

glosses: To bribe.

examples.text: He tried to buy me with gifts, but I wouldn't give up my beliefs.

After Bongino reiterated that Epstein killed himself, he was flooded with responses of disbelief. "WHO has bought the both of you?" one X user asked of Bongino and Patel, referencing the Fox News interview.

glosses: To be equivalent to in value.

examples.text: The dollar doesn't buy as much as it used to.

glosses: to accept as true; to believe

examples.text: I'm not going to buy your stupid excuses anymore!
People like to say that dead people look asleep, and maybe she would have bought that under different circumstances.

glosses: To make a purchase or purchases, to treat (for a drink, meal or gift)

examples.text: She buys for Federated.
Let's go out for dinner. I'm buying.

glosses: To make a bluff, usually a large one.

examples.text: Smith tried to buy the pot on the river with a huge bluff.

glosses: Something which is bought; a purchase.

examples.text: At only $30, the second-hand kitchen table was a great buy.

glosses: The acquisition of title to, or property in, anything for a price; buying for money or its equivalent.

examples.text: They offer a free hamburger with the purchase of a drink.

glosses: That which is obtained for a price in money or its equivalent.

examples.text: He was pleased with his latest purchase.

[Said by a shopkeeper] I really don't think you can carry any more purchases. You can come again after you sell something, or you can simply discard an item to lighten your load. Or, you might want to sell the things you don't need here!

glosses: That which is obtained, got or acquired, in any manner, honestly or dishonestly; property; possession; acquisition.

examples.text: I'll […] get meat to save thee, / Or lose my life i’ th’ purchase.

glosses: A price paid for a house or estate, etc. equal to the amount of the rent or income during the stated number of years.

examples.text: Suppose a freehold house to be worth 20 years’ purchase […]

glosses: Any mechanical hold or advantage, applied to the raising or removing of heavy bodies, as by a lever, a tackle or capstan.

examples.text: It is hard to get purchase on a nail without a pry bar or hammer.
The problem is that the model of individual responsibility assumed by most versions of ethics have little purchase on the behavior of Capital or corporations.

glosses: The apparatus, tackle or device by which such mechanical advantage is gained and (in nautical terminology) the ratio of such a device, like a pulley, or block and tackle.

examples.text: He describes the operation thus: "The heavy ram employed to impart the finishing strokes, hoisted up with double purchase and snail's pace to the summit of the Piling Engine, and then falling down like a thunderbolt on the head of the devoted timber, driving it perhaps a single half inch in to the stratum below, is well calculated to put to the test the virtue of patience, while it illustrates the old adage of—slow and sure."

glosses: The amount of hold one has from an individual foothold or ledge.

examples.text: At first, he was climbing down, testing for purchase with his feet. But soon, as the entire section of ground rotated, he was lifted into the air, and up and down flipped around.

glosses: Acquisition of lands or tenements by means other than descent or inheritance, namely, by one's own act or agreement.

examples.text: The difference […]between the acquisition of an estate by descent and by purchase

glosses: To buy, obtain by payment of a price in money or its equivalent.

examples.text: to purchase land, to purchase a house

glosses: To pursue and obtain; to acquire by seeking; to gain, obtain, or acquire.

examples.text: that loves the thing he cannot purchase
They [the English] are all on fire / To purchaſe from the Spaniard. If their Carracks / Come deeply laden, vvee ſhall tugge vvith them / For golden ſpoile.
Your accent is something finer than you could purchase in so removed a dwelling.

glosses: To obtain by any outlay, as of labor, danger, or sacrifice, etc.

examples.text: to purchase favor with flattery
One poor retiring minute […] / Would purchase thee a thousand thousand friends.

glosses: To expiate by a fine or forfeit.

examples.text: Not tears nor prayers shall purchase out abuses.

glosses: To apply to (anything) a device for obtaining a mechanical advantage; to get a purchase upon, or apply a purchase to; to raise or move by mechanical means.

examples.text: to purchase a cannon

glosses: To put forth effort to obtain anything; to strive; to exert oneself.

examples.text:
1523–1525, John Bourchier, 2nd Baron Berners, Froissart's Chronicles
Duke John of Brabant purchased greatly that the Earl of Flanders should have his daughter in marriage.

glosses: To constitute the buying power for a purchase, have a trading value.

examples.text: Many aristocratic refugees' portable treasures purchased their safe passage and comfortable exile during the revolution.

glosses: Something (usually money) given in exchange for influence or as an inducement to breaking the law.

Undue reward for anything against justice is a bribe.
The bribes I took did not influence me to become evil. I was evil from the beginning and the bribes were merely a bonus

glosses: The act of offering or paying such a payment: an act of bribery.
That which seduces; seduction; allurement.

examples.text: Not the bribes of sordid wealth can seduce to leave these everblooming sweets.
Remy, this was a bribe! Our whole marriage has been nothing but a series of bribes!

examples.text: She was accused of trying to bribe the jury into making false statements.

glosses: To gain by a bribe; to induce as by a bribe.

glosses: To induce (someone) to commit an unlawful or malicious act, especially in a corrupt manner.

examples.text: Till thou to ſpit the venome of thy ſpite, / Subornedſt Cupid how he ſoone might ſlay me, / Abandoning his bowe and arrowes quite, / You laid his priuie complot to betray me; […]

[H]ee ſuborneth one named Saulus and the ſouldiers of the Ievves to follovv the Gothes hard at the heeles, vvho killing ſome thouſands of them, oportunitie beeing offered, might by that meanes exaſperat at the mindes of the people and mooue them to breake the league.

glosses: To induce (someone) to commit an unlawful or malicious act, especially in a corrupt manner.
To induce (someone, such as a witness) to commit perjury, for example by making a false accusation or giving false evidence.

examples.text: [Y]ou shall finde their tongues chayned to another mans trencher, and as it were, Knights of the Post, suborned to say, sweare and stare the uttermost they can, as those that passe not what they say, nor with what face they say it, so they say no truth.
By heauen (fond vvretch) yͧ knovvſt not vvhat thou ſpeak'ſt, / Or elſe thou art ſuborn'd againſt his honor / In hatefull practiſe: […]
Thou that bribeſt a corrupt Officer, ſuborneſt a perjured vvitneſs, procureſt a packt Jury, […] couldſt thou be patient thy ſelf to be vvreſted out of thy ovvn apparent right by ſuch engines?
[I]n the heat of their quarrel there came in a witness suborned by some of Mariamne's enemies, who accused her to the king [Herod the Great] of a design to poison him.
[A]n attempt to suborn a person to commit perjury, upon a reference to the judges, was unanimously holden by them to be a misdemeanor.

Boethius, again, says that the Gothic courtiers hated him, and suborned branded scoundrels to swear away his life and that of the senate, because he had opposed 'the hounds of the palace,' Amigast, Trigulla, and other greedy barbarians.

glosses: To achieve (some result; specifically, perjury) in a corrupt manner.

examples.text: [U]pon ſingle Perjuries ſuborned by themſelves they condemned Men unheard, and ſold their Eſtates vvithout ſuffering them to ſpeak for themſelves— […]

glosses: To procure or provide (something) secretly and often in a dishonest manner.

examples.text: In a golden bowl / She then suborn'd a potion, in her soul / Deform'd things thinking; for amidst the wine / She mix'd her man-transforming medicine; […]
Firm we ſubſiſt, yet poſſible to ſwerve, / Since Reaſon not impoſſibly may meet / Some ſpecious object by the Foe ſubornd, […]
Behold of ev'ry age; ripe manhood ſee, / Decrepit years, and helpleſs infancy: / Thoſe who, by lingring ſickneſs, loſe their breath; / And thoſe vvho, by deſpair, ſuborn their death: […]

Be ready at my Call, my choſen fevv / VVith arms adminiſter'd ſhall aid thy Crevv. / Then entring unexpected vvill vve ſeize / Our deſtin'd Prey, from Men diſſolv'd in eaſe; / By VVine diſabled, unprepar'd for Fight; / And haſt'ning to the Seas ſuborn our Flight: […]

From this curſt hour, the fraudful dame / Of ſacred Truth uſurps the name, / And, vvith a vile, perfidious mind, / Roams far and near, to chat mankind; / Falſe ſighs ſuborns, and artful tears, / And ſtarts vvith vain pretended fears; […]

glosses: To make use of (something), especially for corrupt or dishonest reasons.

examples.text: Nor is he onely content to ſuborne Divine Juſtice in his cenſure of vvhat is paſt, but he aſſumes the perſon of Chriſt himſelf to prognoſticate over us vvhat he vviſhes vvould come.

glosses: To aid, assist, or support (something).

translations.source_sense_description: подкупить

glosses: Gâter, altérer, changer en mal.

examples.text: Il allait quelquefois chez Zadig, et se mettait à table sans être prié : il y corrompait toute la joie de la société, comme on dit que les harpies infectent les viandes qu'elles touchent.
Le bonheur de t'avoir est toujours corrompu par la perspective de te perdre.
La viande se corrompt par les grandes chaleurs.
La langue latine commença à se corrompre peu de temps après Auguste.

glosses: Séduire, débaucher.

examples.text: Il fut tué par un des siens dont il avait voulu corrompre la femme.
Socrate fut accusé de corrompre la jeunesse.

glosses: Engager quelqu'un par des dons, des promesses, ou par d'autres moyens, à faire, ou ne pas faire, quelque chose contre son devoir, sa conscience, contre l'honneur, etc.

examples.text: La justice est faussée, et ceux qui élèvent la voix au nom du peuple, on les corrompt ou on les supprime, et ceux qui le servent le volent.

glosses: Plier, rompre à force de plier.

examples.text: Corrompre un métal, un cuir.

translations.source_sense_description: подкупить

glosses: Égarer, abuser, faire tomber dans l’erreur par ses insinuations, par ses écrits, par ses discours, par ses exemples, etc.

examples.text: Privé de tout accommodement, de ses fards, de ses sourires et de ses ruses, le vice a peu de chance de séduire la vertu la plus chancelante.
Cet hypocrite séduisait les peuples.
Il l’a séduit par ses maximes pernicieuses.
Cela ne peut séduire que les hommes simples et ignorants.
Le faux espoir qui nous avait séduits.

glosses: Faire tomber en faute ; suborner ; corrompre ; débaucher.

examples.text: Notre moniteur avait entretenu une liaison épisodique avec Sylvia du temps où elle habitait en région parisienne. […]. Il semble que ce don Juan des courts ait profité de sa fonction professorale pour séduire un grand nombre de ses élèves.
Séduire des témoins. — Séduire des domestiques pour les faire parler contre leur maître.

glosses: Convaincre de commencer une relation amoureuse.

examples.text: Ainsi s'affirme, incoercible, le besoin réflexe d'ajuster notre condition à ce qu'elle est et non de suivre l’exclamation superlative des vertiges forains et des boules à facettes des bals pour séduire les filles.

glosses: Toucher, plaire, persuader.

examples.text: Ne faites pas aller et venir une asperge dans votre bouche en regardant languissamment le jeune homme que vous voulez séduire.
Je ne sais pas si Jean-Louis Darc séduisit ma mère ou si ce fut elle qui s'en éprit la première, mais je crois que Céline Thiébault désira ce grand gaillard, cette vigueur animale.
Cet homme m’a séduit par la franchise de son langage.
Sa bonté séduit tous les cœurs.
Ses manières m’ont séduit.

glosses: Il s’emploie absolument, surtout dans la dernière acception.

examples.text: C’est un homme habile à séduire.
Cela séduit.
Son ton séduit.

translations.source_sense_description: взять в прикупе

glosses: kupić

examples.text: Он купи́л дорогу́ю маши́ну.

glosses: Acheter, acquérir.
satın almak, almak
買，購買 [接 賓格 「某物」 和 與格 「給某人」]

examples.text: Я хочу́ кое-что́ купи́ть.
Он сказал им в ответ: вы дайте им есть. И сказали Ему: разве нам пойти купить хлеба динариев на двести и дать им есть?
examples.translation: 耶穌回答說：「你們給他們吃吧！」門徒說：「我們可以去買二十兩銀子的餅給他們吃嗎？」
